assessment: Checked all extraction docs (9 functionalities, 11 instructions, 11 config/infra, 6 flows) against the pinned stack: FastAPI 0.123.10 on Python 3.10, PostgreSQL 16.15, pytest 8.3.3, Kotlin/Jetpack Compose Android client (com.nexti.minisoporte). No nwiki/ exists (greenfield). Phase A surfaced missing definitions around user provisioning, token mechanics, data access, rate limiting, Android networking, minSdk, pagination, and sign-out semantics. Phase B verified versions via live sources: (1) VERSION COMPATIBILITY — PyPI shows FastAPI 0.123.10 is real (Dec 5, 2025) and the current release is 0.142.2 (Sep 30, 2026); both require Python >=3.10 and Pydantic v2, so the pin is valid but one year behind; passlib is unmaintained since 1.7.4 (Oct 8, 2020) and breaks with bcrypt >= 4.1 per pyca/bcrypt issue #684 ('AttributeError: module bcrypt has no attribute __about__'), so the classic FastAPI passlib-bcrypt pairing must be avoided; PyJWT is actively maintained (2.15.1, Sep 28, 2026); SQLAlchemy 2.0.54 is the maintenance series and 2.1.3 (Oct 2, 2026) the current series per sqlalchemy.org/download.html. (2) CROSS-LIBRARY PAIRINGS — passlib 1.7.4 vs bcrypt 4.x is the one verified breakage; SQLAlchemy 2.0.x/2.1.x + Alembic and PyJWT + FastAPI 0.123.x/Pydantic v2 have no known incompatibilities. (3) ARCHITECTURE FIT — the layered, DI-based FastAPI structure fits SQLAlchemy 2.0-style sessions and Pydantic v2 schemas with no friction. (4) INFRASTRUCTURE/DEPLOYMENT — internal-testing only with no cloud infra selected, so an in-process rate limiter suffices; no Redis/worker tier exists in the target plan. (5) SCALE-SENSITIVE CHOICES — single-employee-base internal tool: unbounded incident lists and in-memory state are acceptable for v1 but pagination behavior should be decided explicitly. On Android, Maven Central shows Retrofit 3.0.0 (May 2025, Kotlin-first) as current over the 2.x line, and Google Maven shows Compose BOM 2026.09.00 as current. Findings below are ordered: missing definitions first, then compatibility decisions.

questions.question: How are employee and support accounts provisioned, since no registration endpoint, admin screen, or user-management flow exists in v1 and the seed only creates demo accounts in non-production?
questions.rationale: FUNC-009 only seeds one demo employee and one demo support agent in development; INSTR-010 forbids seeding in production. Without a stated provisioning path, real employees in the internal-test deployment have no way to get an account or password.
options: Out of scope for v1 — operations inserts users directly into the User table via SQL/scripts
Documented CLI management command (e.g. create-user script) reading password from environment variables
Extend the demo seed so the internal-test environment also runs it manually with configured emails
Add an authenticated admin-only user-creation endpoint to the API in v1
Other
questions.recommended: Documented CLI management command (e.g. create-user script) reading password from environment variables
questions.runner_up: Out of scope for v1 — operations inserts users directly into the User table via SQL/scripts

questions.question: What concrete token format and expiration should the signed session token use?
questions.rationale: CONF-001 mandates signed tokens with expiration and signature validation but does not name a format or lifetime; the Android client (CONF-002) stores one token with no refresh flow, so the TTL decides how often employees are forced to sign in again.
options: JWT (HS256) with 8-hour expiration, no refresh token
JWT (HS256) with 24-hour expiration, no refresh token
JWT (HS256) with 30-minute access token plus refresh-token endpoint
Opaque random token with server-side session table and expiry column
Other
questions.recommended: JWT (HS256) with 8-hour expiration, no refresh token
questions.runner_up: JWT (HS256) with 24-hour expiration, no refresh token

questions.question: Which data-access and migration approach should the backend use for PostgreSQL 16.15?
questions.rationale: CONF-005 allows 'parameterized queries or ORM' and CONF-008 requires reproducible migrations, but neither an ORM nor a migration tool is named. SQLAlchemy's download page (checked Oct 2026) shows 2.0.54 as the maintenance series and 2.1.3 as the current series, so a series must be picked deliberately.
options: SQLAlchemy 2.0.x ORM (maintenance series, 2.0.54) + Alembic migrations
SQLAlchemy 2.1.x ORM (current series, 2.1.3) + Alembic migrations
Raw asyncpg/psycopg parameterized SQL + plain SQL migration scripts applied in order
Raw parameterized SQL + Alembic managing schema without ORM models
Other
alt_values: Raw asyncpg/psycopg parameterized SQL + plain SQL migration scripts applied in order

questions.question: How should rate limiting on POST /api/auth/login be implemented, given no cache/Redis tier exists in the target plan?
questions.rationale: CONF-003 requires throttling of failed sign-in attempts without leaking account existence, but no limiter technology is named. The target plan has only FastAPI + PostgreSQL, so the limiter's state store is an open infrastructure decision.
options: In-process in-memory limiter (per-IP and per-email counters) built with FastAPI dependencies
slowapi (Starlette rate-limit library) with in-memory backend
PostgreSQL-backed attempt table with time-window queries (survives restarts, multi-worker safe)
In-memory limiter in v1 plus a documented upgrade path to a shared store if multi-worker deployment arrives
Other
questions.recommended: In-process in-memory limiter (per-IP and per-email counters) built with FastAPI dependencies
questions.runner_up: PostgreSQL-backed attempt table with time-window queries (survives restarts, multi-worker safe)

questions.question: Which HTTP client and JSON serialization stack should the Android app use to call the REST API?
questions.rationale: CONF-011 defines the API surface and the mobile contract fixes Kotlin/Compose, but no networking or serialization library is named; the token header, error parsing, and retry paths (CONF-009) all depend on this choice.
options: Retrofit + OkHttp + kotlinx.serialization converter
Retrofit + OkHttp + Moshi converter
Ktor Client with kotlinx.serialization (Compose-idiomatic, coroutine-native)
OkHttp direct calls with kotlinx.serialization and no Retrofit layer
Other

questions.question: Which Android minSdk should the app target (the wizard leaves the recommended minimum unpinned)?
questions.rationale: The mobile delivery contract requires 'the supported recommended minimum' but records no API level, and the value must be pinned in app/build.gradle.kts. Jetpack Compose requires API 21+, and modern AndroidX/Compose tooling works best at 24+; the choice affects internal-test device coverage.
options: minSdk 26 (Android 8.0) — modern baseline, covers most active devices
minSdk 24 (Android 7.0) — wider coverage, still safe with Compose
minSdk 29 (Android 10) — strictest, only if company devices are known-recent
minSdk 21 (Android 5.0) — maximum coverage, older support burden
Other
questions.recommended: minSdk 26 (Android 8.0) — modern baseline, covers most active devices
questions.runner_up: minSdk 24 (Android 7.0) — wider coverage, still safe with Compose

questions.question: Should GET /api/incidents return all of the employee's incidents in v1, or support pagination?
questions.rationale: FUNC-003 and CONF-011 define only an optional status filter, newest-first; no page size, cursor, or offset is specified anywhere. Deciding now prevents an unplanned API-shape change later while keeping v1 simple.
options: No pagination in v1 — return all owned incidents matching the filter, newest first
Server-side limit/offset (e.g. ?limit=50&offset=0) with total count in the response
No pagination in v1 but reserve query-parameter names (limit/offset) and document them
Cursor-based pagination keyed on created_at/id from the start
Other
questions.recommended: No pagination in v1 — return all owned incidents matching the filter, newest first
questions.runner_up: No pagination in v1 but reserve query-parameter names (limit/offset) and document them

questions.question: Does sign-out require server-side token invalidation, or is deleting the local token sufficient?
questions.rationale: FUNC-002 only mandates deleting the locally stored token, and CONF-001 mandates signed expiring tokens; if tokens remain valid server-side until expiry, a signed-out device's token still works if copied. This is a security posture decision the extractions leave ambiguous.
options: Client-side deletion only — stateless JWT valid until expiry (matches FUNC-002 literally)
Client-side deletion plus short token TTL (e.g. 8h) accepted as the mitigation
Server-side revocation list (jti denylist in PostgreSQL checked on each request)
Stateless JWT with a token-version claim stored on the User row, bumped to invalidate all sessions
Other
questions.recommended: Client-side deletion plus short token TTL (e.g. 8h) accepted as the mitigation
questions.runner_up: Client-side deletion only — stateless JWT valid until expiry (matches FUNC-002 literally)

questions.question: FastAPI 0.123.10 (pinned in the target plan, released Dec 5, 2025) is now a year behind the current 0.142.2 (Sep 30, 2026 per PyPI) — should the project keep the exact pin or move to the latest 0.142.x patch line?
questions.rationale: PyPI release history (checked Oct 2026) shows 0.123.10 as the final 0.123.x patch and 0.142.2 as current; both lines require Python >=3.10 and Pydantic v2, so either works with the pinned runtime, but 0.123.x receives no further fixes. The target plan is the source of truth, so staying put should be an explicit decision.
options: Keep exactly FastAPI 0.123.10 as the target plan mandates
Use the latest 0.142.x (0.142.2) since the plan's '0.123.10' is a point-in-time snapshot
Keep 0.123.10 for v1 and add a tracked task to review the upgrade before any production rollout
Other
questions.recommended: Keep exactly FastAPI 0.123.10 as the target plan mandates
questions.runner_up: Keep 0.123.10 for v1 and add a tracked task to review the upgrade before any production rollout

questions.question: Which password-hashing implementation should store password_hash, given that the common passlib+bcrypt pairing is broken?
questions.rationale: Verified via pyca/bcrypt issue #684 (open): passlib 1.7.4 — last released Oct 8, 2020 per PyPI — raises 'AttributeError: module bcrypt has no attribute __about__' with bcrypt 4.1+ (the FastAPI documentation's classic snippet). The project must hash with a maintained library directly.
options: argon2-cffi (Argon2id — OWASP password-storage first choice, actively maintained)
bcrypt library used directly (no passlib), current 4.x
passlib 1.7.4 with bcrypt pinned < 4.1 (explicitly accepting an unmaintained stack)
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 via hashlib (stdlib, no dependency)
Other
questions.recommended: bcrypt library used directly (no passlib), current 4.x
questions.runner_up: argon2-cffi (Argon2id — OWASP password-storage first choice, actively maintained)
alt_values: argon2-cffi (Argon2id — OWASP password-storage first choice, actively maintained)

questions.question: Which JWT library should sign and validate the session tokens?
questions.rationale: PyPI (checked Sep/Oct 2026) shows PyJWT at 2.15.1 released Sep 28, 2026, production/stable, supporting Python 3.9+ including 3.10 — actively maintained. The alternative most FastAPI tutorials use, python-jose, has long gaps between releases, so the choice should be deliberate rather than copied from tutorials.
options: PyJWT (actively released, 2.15.1) with HS256 and explicit algorithms allow-list on decode
python-jose (the older FastAPI tutorial standard)
Authlib (broader OAuth/JWS toolkit, heavier than needed for simple HS256)
python-jwt
Other
questions.recommended: PyJWT (actively released, 2.15.1) with HS256 and explicit algorithms allow-list on decode
questions.runner_up: Authlib (broader OAuth/JWS toolkit, heavier than needed for simple HS256)

questions.question: Retrofit released a Kotlin-first 3.0.0 (May 2025 per Maven Central) after the 2.x line ended at 2.11.0 — which major version should the Android client adopt?
questions.rationale: Maven Central metadata for com.squareup.retrofit2:retrofit (fetched Oct 2026) shows latest/release 3.0.0 with 2.12.0 the last 2.x point release. Retrofit 3.0.0 is the going-forward line with built-in Kotlin support, but 2.11/2.12 remains battle-tested if maximum familiarity is preferred.
options: Retrofit 3.0.0 (current release line, Kotlin-first) + OkHttp 5.x + kotlinx.serialization
Retrofit 2.12.0 (last 2.x point release, most tutorial coverage) + OkHttp 4.x
Skip Retrofit entirely — Ktor Client 3.x with kotlinx.serialization
Other
questions.recommended: Retrofit 3.0.0 (current release line, Kotlin-first) + OkHttp 5.x + kotlinx.serialization
questions.runner_up: Skip Retrofit entirely — Ktor Client 3.x with kotlinx.serialization
alt_values: Retrofit 2.12.0 (last 2.x point release, most tutorial coverage) + OkHttp 4.x

questions.question: Which Jetpack Compose BOM generation should the build pin, given the current BOM moves monthly?
questions.rationale: Google Maven metadata for androidx.compose:compose-bom (fetched Oct 2026) lists 2026.09.00 as the current release with the 2025.x line (through 2025.12.01) still available. Pinning an arbitrary older BOM loses stable fixes; pinning the newest couples the build to the bleeding edge, so the generation should be an explicit decision for a reproducible internal build.
options: Latest stable BOM (2026.09.00) with a pinned lockfile-style version catalog
Last of the 2025 line (2025.12.01) — one year of stabilization
Whatever BOM ships with the Android Studio version used internally, documented in the design
Other
questions.recommended: Latest stable BOM (2026.09.00) with a pinned lockfile-style version catalog
questions.runner_up: Last of the 2025 line (2025.12.01) — one year of stabilization
